body:
If one removes the following line in ports/boost/portfile.cmake, it works again.

`file(APPEND ${CURRENT_PACKAGES_DIR}/include/boost/config/user.hpp "\n#define BOOST_AUTO_LINK_NOMANGLE\n")`

This line was added as part of 56c3febc9de168df0707269e48d31701f60e7673 in order to enable boost's system install (= library names without mangled suffixes).

This option was later disabled in ff4d33b156e06b5457837361b28803fb8570d350 but the line setting `BOOST_AUTO_LINK_NOMANGLE` was kept.

I'm not sure if removing this line will work across all projects but at least Wt builds again and I'll be testing a few more ports.

This also fixes the build for cpprestsdk (and probably others).
I'll prepare a PR.

Yes, it's 100% intended to build vcpkg on your local machine! 

The error messages you received ("Could not run script...")[1] are caused by a failure while running:
```
>powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Command "& {& 'C:\vcpkg\scripts\findVisualStudioInstallationInstances.ps1' }" 2>&1
```

Could you try running that command in verbose mode (listed below) and post the results?
```
>powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Command "& {& 'C:\vcpkg\scripts\findVisualStudioInstallationInstances.ps1' -verbose }"
```


It's possible that NuGet failed to download Microsoft.VisualStudio.Setup.Configuration.Native due to a proxy issue.
